Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. There will be a brief pause while registration is processed. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge Inc.'s second quarter fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; and Lisa Wong, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge Inc.'s performance for the second quarter. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge Copilot and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: enhancing sales efficiency, growing average contract value, optimizing our operating expense profile, and maintaining a disciplined capital allocation strategy.

On sales efficiency, we continued to compress our sales cycles and improve conversion rates across the board, reflecting the strength of our go-to-market execution.

In terms of average contract value, we saw robust expansion, particularly in our enterprise segment, fueled by deeper product adoption and AI integrations.

We also made meaningful progress in operating expense management, delivering leverage while investing aggressively in innovation.

And on capital allocation, our strong balance sheet allowed us to prioritize high-return opportunities across organic growth, tuck-in acquisitions, and shareholder returns.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $152 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $24 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, with approximately $1.2 billion in cash and short-term investments at quarter-end, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

Let me now turn to our core SaaS metrics, starting with average contract value, or ACV. I'm pleased to report that ACV reached $52,300 in Q2, marking a robust 22% year-over-year increase from $42,800, and a sequential 7% rise from $48,900 in Q1. This acceleration underscores the strength of our land-and-expand model and our strategic pivot toward high-value enterprise deployments, even amidst broader market headwinds like elevated interest rates compressing SMB budgets.

Our ACV calculation normalizes the total contract value over a 12-month period, excluding one-time professional services fees, which aligns with industry standards as seen in peers like Snowflake or Databricks. Breaking it down by key drivers and segments: In the enterprise cohort with over $1 million ARR, ACV averaged $185,000, up 28% year-over-year, driven by a 15-point increase in module adoption rates, particularly with our AI-powered DevSecOps suite, CloudForge Sentinel, which bundles autonomous vulnerability scanning and predictive deployment analytics. We've converted 62% of new logos in this segment to multi-module contracts at signing, up from 45% a year ago.

Mid-market ACV, for $100,000 to $1 million ARR customers, grew 19% to $78,500, fueled by targeted expansions with net revenue retention of 118%, reflecting successful cross-sells into our usage-based analytics add-on, Forge Insights, which leverages real-time cost optimization akin to Datadog's Cloud Cost Management. SMB ACV under $100,000 ARR remained stable at $22,400, up just 4%, offset by a 25% increase in self-serve conversions via our freemium-to-paid funnel.

Overall, new customer ACV expanded 25% to $49,200, while existing customer ACV grew 20% through expansions and renewals, validating our 125% dollar-based net revenue retention for the quarter. Key accelerators include our GenAI integrations, like Sentinel's AI-driven code review reducing deployment failures by up to 40%, boosting ACV by an average of $15,000 per deal. We've shifted 35% of contracts to hybrid usage-based pricing with committed minimums plus overages, unlocking 1.8 times higher ACV than fixed-price renewals.

Regionally, North America, 74% of ACV, grew 24%, led by hyperscaler partnerships with AWS and Azure and deals in fintech and healthcare commanding premiums for compliance modules. EMEA, 18% of ACV, rose 30% to $55,000 average, benefiting from GDPR tailwinds and our Berlin data center. APAC, 8% of ACV, saw 12% growth to $42,100, with traction in Japan manufacturing via IoT tools.

These trends outpace the industry average ACV growth of about 15% per Bessemer Venture Partners' Cloud Index, as we focus on sticky, high-ROI outcomes with LTV-to-CAC ratios exceeding 5-to-1. Looking forward, we expect Q3 ACV in the $54,000 to $56,000 range, with upside from Forge Horizon, our agentic AI platform for CI/CD orchestration.

Next, let's dive into our operating expense breakdown, where we continue to balance aggressive growth investments with improving efficiency, hitting a Rule of 40 score of 52 this quarter on 28% growth and 24% adjusted operating margin. Total operating expenses were $118 million, or 78% of revenue, down 200 basis points year-over-year, driven by operating leverage.

Starting with R&D at $48 million, or 32% of revenue, up 35% year-over-year. This reflects heavy investment in next-generation capabilities, including doubling down on generative AI with CloudForge Copilot, a multimodal AI agent automating 40% of routine workflow tasks, tailored for cross-functional teams like Adobe Sensei or Salesforce Einstein. Engineering headcount grew 25% to 450, with 60% on core platform and 40% on agentic AI and zero-trust security. Our EMEA R&D hub in Dublin ramped 50% year-over-year for GDPR-compliant models, and APAC investments in Bangalore yield wins in edge computing for Japan and India. R&D ticked up 100 basis points sequentially but should peak at 30-32% through fiscal 2025 before stabilizing.

Sales and marketing was $54 million, or 35% of revenue, up 18% but down 400 basis points as a percentage. CAC payback dropped to 16 months from 20, with CAC ratio at 0.85 times on a trailing 12-month basis. 55% of new ARR came from product-led growth channels with viral coefficients above 1.2. Field sales expanded 15% to 320 reps, with productivity up 22%. Marketing focused on digital performance channels like LinkedIn, yielding 3 times ROI. EMEA sales grew 45% on regulatory tailwinds, APAC at 20% with reallocation to SEA. S&M should decline to 32-34% by fiscal 2026 as NRR from Copilot drives expansions.

G&A at $16 million, or 10.5% of revenue, flat year-over-year and down 150 basis points. Non-comp expenses held steady via vendor consolidation and remote-first policies. Stock-based comp rose 5% to $8 million, aligning with peers. We've optimized US headcount for 15% growth versus 28% revenue growth, building compliance for EU AI Act. G&A trends toward 9% long-term, supporting 30% free cash flow margins.

Now, on sales efficiency, specifically sales cycle length and conversion rates, which are cornerstones of our leverage. Our enterprise-weighted average sales cycle improved to 92 days, down 23% year-over-year from 120 days and ahead of the SaaS median of 105 days per Bessemer.

By segment: Enterprise over $250,000 ACV at 145 days, down from 180, with pilots closing 40% faster via AI-driven ROI calculators. Mid-market $50,000 to $250,000 ACV at 65 days from 85, via hybrid inside sales boosting meeting bookings 35%. SMB/self-serve under $50,000 ACV at 28 days, with 60% PLG conversions from freemium.

Regionally: North America 85 days, EMEA 115 days compressing 15% via localized teams, APAC 105 days improving 20% with Tokyo office. Conversion rates: overall MQL-to-closed-won at 12.5%, up from 9.2%. MQL-to-SQL 28% up 300 basis points via intent data from 6sense; SQL-to-opportunity 42%, enterprise 55%; opportunity-to-close 32% up 400 basis points via Gong analysis.

Gains from tech stack like Chorus.ai, PLG at 35% of new ARR with 1.3x viral coefficient, AE quota attainment 112%, and macro resilience. Expect under 90 days enterprise-wide in fiscal 2025 with sales tech reinvestments.

Turning to our capital allocation strategy, which remains a cornerstone of our disciplined approach to driving long-term shareholder value. We ended the quarter with $1.2 billion in cash and short-term investments, and approximately $450 million in free cash flow for the full year to date, up 28% year-over-year. Our net debt is effectively zero, giving flexibility while adhering to Rule of 40 at 42% this quarter.

We prioritize high-ROI investments accelerating land-and-expand, enhancing CloudForge AI Core—our flagship analytics and collaboration suite—and expanding our $150 billion TAM in enterprise workflow automation. We target returns exceeding our 9% WACC, benchmarked to ServiceNow and Workday, in a market with SaaS multiples at 7-9 times EV/ARR.

Three buckets: Organic investments, 65% of capex and opex or $320 million. R&D at 22% of revenue doubles down on AI, with $150 million for multimodal capabilities integrating large language models like GitHub Copilot, improving query times 40% and AI add-ons at 15% of new ARR from 5%. North America 68% of ARR, APAC $50 million for localization driving 35% growth, EMEA 22% with 65% win rates over $1 million ACV, LATAM pilot $20 million. Sales and marketing 18%, CAC payback 14 months via ABM and 500,000 developer community.

M&A, 20% or $180 million across two tuck-ins. $120 million for DataForge Analytics, $25 million ARR in predictive analytics integrating graph neural networks, $10 million synergies, 30% attach rates. $60 million for EuroComply in EU AI Act tools, EMEA ARR ramping 50%. Pipeline of 10 diligences in AI agents, verticals like healthcare, at 6-8 times ARR.

Shareholder returns, 35% of FCF or $155 million: $120 million buybacks at 15% discount to intrinsic value, $35 million dividend at $0.10 quarterly yielding 0.5%, 25% payout ratio.

Forward, $500 million-plus FCF in 2024, 70% to R&D, $800 million dry powder for M&A. This delivered 150% TSR over three years, outperforming SaaS index by 40%, excited for AI-SaaS adding $1 trillion by 2028 per McKinsey.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $600 million to $620 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge Copilot on your overall growth?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge Copilot has been transformative, automating 40% of routine tasks and driving significant upsell opportunities. It's contributed to 15% of new ARR already, accelerating our NRR to 125% and helping land larger enterprise deals with 62% multi-module adoption at signing. We're seeing it shorten pilots by 40% and boost ACV by $15,000 on average, positioning us strongly against competitors.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Lisa Wong:
Thanks, Emily. International remains a high priority, with APAC and EMEA growing faster than North America. We've invested $50 million in APAC localization, launching support in key languages and driving 35% YoY growth via partnerships with AWS and Azure. In EMEA, GDPR features and the EuroComply acquisition have boosted win rates to 65% and ARR ramping 50% QoQ. We're piloting LATAM with $20 million for integrations, targeting a $10 billion TAM. Overall, we aim for 25% international growth this year, with new hubs in Singapore and expanded Tokyo presence.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Mike Patel:
Good question, David. Churn remains low at under 5% gross, supporting our 118% NRR. In this environment, we've focused on proactive customer success, with expansions offsetting any contraction—85% of bookings were net new or upsells. Our AI tools like Copilot deliver sticky value, reducing deployment failures and proving ROI quickly. We've also enhanced renewal processes with dedicated teams and usage-based pricing to align with customer spend, keeping dollar net expansion at 25%.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
